Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verses 1–6:

The fifth volume of Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman fi Tafsir Kalam al-Mannan
By the Imam, the learned scholar, our shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasir ibn Sa'di, may Allah forgive him. Amin.
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
All praise is due to Allah, and I invoke blessings and peace upon Muhammad, his family and his companions.
To proceed: since the science of tafsir (exegesis) of the Qur'an is the most noble of sciences absolutely and the most important, and the most deserving of verifying its meanings and understanding its structures, because it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy, which He sent down as guidance and mercy for the servants, and as an explanation of everything and a detailing of all that they need in their religion, their worldly life and their hereafter; and since it is among the special features of the knowledge of the Qur'an that understanding part of it, and a portion of it, helps in understanding all of it; because the Qur'an, from its beginning to its end, revolves around establishing beneficial principles, great realities and laws, good rulings and sound beliefs, directs the servants to every good, warns them against every evil, and repeats and displays these matters with varied methods and suitable variations, in the utmost ease, simplicity, firmness, and a manner that cannot be improved upon.
The question has been repeatedly put to me by many companions regarding publishing this tafsir of ours in its entirety, and they insisted because of the great benefit they see in it. I excused myself, saying that this is very difficult, because it is extensive; and also, in these times the desire of people for lengthy books has decreased. Therefore I wished to answer them by publishing part of what they requested, which is limiting it to one part of the parts of this tafsir. The choice fell on the middle part, from the surah of al-Kahf to the end of al-Naml; what cannot be obtained in its entirety should not be abandoned in its entirety.
I hope from Allah, and I ask Him, to make it sincerely for His face, beneficial for us and for our brothers, and to support us with His help, care and success; indeed He is the Generous, the Noble, the Kind, the Merciful.
I have followed it with generalities and principles from the universals of tafsir, to make up for what may escape the reader outside this part; for principles and universals are the foundation upon which branches and particulars are built, and through them benefit and usefulness are obtained, in their brevity, that is not obtained in lengthy discourse. He is sufficient for us and the best Disposer of affairs.
The author.

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

{1} {Al-hamd} (praise): it is the commendation of Him by His attributes, which are all attributes of perfection, and by His apparent and hidden blessings, the religious and the worldly. The greatest of His blessings absolutely is His sending down the Great Book upon His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). So He praised Himself, and implicit in it is guiding the servants to praise Him for sending the Messenger to them and sending down the Book upon them. Then He described this Book with two attributes that indicate it is perfect in every respect: negation of crookedness (ʿiwaj) from it, and affirmation that it is upright and straight (qayyim mustaqim). Negation of crookedness requires that there is no falsehood in its reports, and no injustice or futility in its commands and prohibitions. Affirmation of straightness requires that it does not inform or command except with the most exalted reports, which fill hearts with knowledge, faith and understanding, such as reporting the names, attributes and actions of Allah, and among them the unseen matters, past and future; and that its commands and prohibitions purify souls, cleanse them, develop them and perfect them, because they include complete justice, equity, sincerity and worship of Allah, the Lord of the worlds, alone, with no partner. It is fitting for a Book described by what has been mentioned that Allah praise Himself for sending it down, and that He extol Himself to His servants by it.

{2} His saying: {to warn of severe punishment from Him} (li-yundhira basan shadidan min ladunh); i.e., that by this noble Qur'an He may warn of His punishment that is with Him, i.e., His decree and judgment upon those who oppose His command, and this includes the punishment of this world and the punishment of the hereafter. This too is among His blessings, that He caused His servants to fear and warned them of what would harm and destroy them; as He said, when He mentioned in this Qur'an the description of the Fire: {This is what Allah makes His servants fear. O My servants, fear Me} (Qur'an 39:16). So from His mercy to His servants is that He has prepared severe punishments for those who oppose His command, has made them clear to them, and has explained to them the causes that lead to them. {And to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds, that for them is a good reward} (ajran hasanan); i.e., and Allah sent down the Book upon His servant to give good tidings to the believers in it and in His messengers and His books, whose faith is complete, and so He made obligatory for them the doing of righteous deeds, which are righteous actions, obligatory and recommended, that combine sincerity and following the Prophet's example. {That for them is a good reward}: it is the reward that Allah ordained for faith and righteous action, and the greatest and most exalted of it is attaining the good pleasure of Allah and entering Paradise, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has occurred to the heart of a human. In describing it as "good" is an indication that there is no troubling or spoiling in it in any way; for if anything of that were found in it, its goodness would not be complete.

{3} Along with that, this good reward is {wherein they will remain forever} (makithina fihi abadan): it does not leave them nor do they leave it; rather their bliss increases at every moment. In mentioning good tidings is an implication of mentioning the deeds that bring about what is announced as good news, namely that this Qur'an has comprised every righteous deed that leads to what souls rejoice in and spirits are delighted by.

{4–5} {And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son"}: from among the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists, who uttered this abominable statement; for they did not say it out of knowledge or certainty; they had no knowledge, nor did their forefathers whom they imitated and followed. Rather, they follow nothing but conjecture and what the souls desire. {Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths} (kabura kalimatan takhruju min afwahihim); i.e., its enormity is great and its punishment severe. What enormity is greater than describing Him as taking a son, which implies His deficiency and another's sharing with Him in the characteristics of lordship and divinity, and lying against Him? {Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?} Therefore He said here: {They say nothing but falsehood}; i.e., pure falsehood with no truth in it at all. Consider how He refuted this statement gradually, moving from one thing to something more refuted than it: He first informed that {they have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers}; saying something about Allah without knowledge is undoubtedly forbidden and invalid. Then He informed secondly that it is an ugly, abominable statement, saying: {Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths}. Then He mentioned thirdly its rank of ugliness, which is lying, contrary to truth.

{6} Since the Prophet (ﷺ) was keen upon the guidance of creation, striving in that to the utmost effort, he (ﷺ) would rejoice and be gladdened by the guidance of those who are guided, and would grieve and be sorrowful over the deniers who are astray, out of his compassion for them and mercy toward them; Allah instructed him not to preoccupy himself with grief over those who do not believe in this Qur'an, as He said in the other [verse]: {Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers} (Qur'an 26:3), and He said: {So let not your soul go out in pursuit of them with regret} (Qur'an 35:8), and here He said: {Perhaps you would kill yourself} (fa-la'allaka bakhi'un nafsaka); i.e., destroying it with grief and sorrow over them. That is because your reward is due from Allah, and if Allah knew any good in these people He would have guided them; but He knew that they are fit only for the Fire, so He forsook them and they were not guided. Therefore your preoccupying yourself with grief and sorrow over them has no benefit for you.
In this verse and its like there is a lesson: the one commanded to call creation to Allah must convey the message and strive by every means that leads to guidance, and block the paths of error and misguidance, to the utmost of his ability, while relying upon Allah in that. If they are guided, then good and blessed; otherwise, let him not grieve or be sorrowful, for that weakens the soul and destroys its strength, having no benefit; rather he should continue in the act he was charged with and directed to, and whatever is beyond that is outside his capacity. And since the Prophet (ﷺ) was told by Allah: {Indeed, you do not guide whom you love} (Qur'an 28:56), and Moses (peace be upon him) said: {My Lord, I have no control except over myself and my brother...} (Qur'an 5:25) — the verse — then others are by greater priority and more fitting; Allah said: {So remind, for you are only a reminder; you are not over them a controller} (Qur'an 88:21–22).

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

The question has been repeatedly put to me by many companions regarding publishing this tafsir of ours in its entirety, and they insisted because of the great benefit they see in it. I excused myself, saying that this is very difficult, because it is extensive; and also, in these times the desire of people for lengthy books has decreased. Therefore I wished to answer them by publishing part of what they requested, which is limiting it to one part of the parts of this tafsir. The choice fell on the middle part, from the surah of al-Kahf to the end of al-Naml; what cannot be obtained in its entirety should not be abandoned in its entirety.

**Verses 9–12**

{9} This interrogative carries the sense of negation and prohibition; that is, do not think that the story of the People of the Cave and what befell them is strange among the signs of God or unique in His wisdom, such that it has no like or counterpart. Rather, God has among His wondrous and strange signs many of the same kind as His signs concerning the People of the Cave, and greater than them. God has always shown His servants signs in the horizons and within themselves, through which the truth is distinguished from falsehood and guidance from error. This negation does not mean that the story of the People of the Cave is not among the marvels. It is indeed one of God's wondrous signs. What is meant is that its kind is very numerous. So dwelling on it alone with wonder and amazement is a deficiency in knowledge and intellect. Rather, it is the duty of the believer to reflect upon all of God's signs, to which God has called His servants to reflect, for they are the key to faith and the path to knowledge and certainty. As for their being associated with the cave, which is a hollow in the mountain, {and the ar-Raqim}, that is, the inscribed record in which their names and their story were written, because of their long-lasting association with it.

{10} Then He mentioned their story in summary, and afterwards detailed it, saying: ﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave﴾, that is, the young men. They intended by this to seek protection and safeguard themselves from the trial their people inflicted upon them. ﴿They said: "Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself"﴾, that is, make us firm through it, protect us from evil, and grant us success in what is good. ﴿And facilitate for us a right course in our affair﴾, that is, make easy for us every means that leads to right guidance, and set right for us the matter of our religion and our worldly life. Thus they combined striving and fleeing from the trial to a place where concealment is possible, with their humble supplication and request to God to facilitate their affairs, and their not relying upon themselves or upon creatures.

{11} For this reason God answered their supplication and provided for them what was not in their reckoning. He said: ﴿So We sealed their ears in the cave﴾, that is, We put them to sleep, ﴿for a number of years﴾, which were three hundred and nine years. In this sleep there is a preservation of their hearts from agitation and fear, and a preservation of them from their people. [And that it might be a clear sign.]

{12} ﴿Then We woke them﴾, that is, from their sleep, ﴿that We might know which of the two parties was more accurate in reckoning the period they had remained﴾, that is, that We might know which of them was more precise in measuring the length of their stay. As God the Exalted said: ﴿And thus did We raise them up that they might question one another...﴾, the verse. In knowing the measure of their stay there is precision in reckoning, and recognition of the perfection of God's power, wisdom and mercy. Had they continued in their sleep, no awareness of any of that would have come from their story.

**Verses 9–12**

{9} This interrogative carries the sense of negation and prohibition; that is, do not think that the story of the People of the Cave and what befell them is strange among the signs of God or unique in His wisdom, such that it has no like or counterpart. Rather, God has among His wondrous and strange signs many of the same kind as His signs concerning the People of the Cave, and greater than them. God has always shown His servants signs in the horizons and within themselves, through which the truth is distinguished from falsehood and guidance from error. This negation does not mean that the story of the People of the Cave is not among the marvels. It is indeed one of God's wondrous signs. What is meant is that its kind is very numerous. So dwelling on it alone with wonder and amazement is a deficiency in knowledge and intellect. Rather, it is the duty of the believer to reflect upon all of God's signs, to which God has called His servants to reflect, for they are the key to faith and the path to knowledge and certainty. As for their being associated with the cave, which is a hollow in the mountain, {and the ar-Raqim}, that is, the inscribed record in which their names and their story were written, because of their long-lasting association with it.

{11} For this reason God answered their supplication and provided for them what was not in their reckoning. He said: ﴿So We sealed their ears in the cave﴾, that is, We put them to sleep, ﴿for a number of years﴾, which were three hundred and nine years. {12} ﴿Then We woke them﴾, that is, from their sleep, ﴿that We might know which of the two parties was more accurate in reckoning the period they had remained﴾, that is, that We might know which of them was more precise in measuring the length of their stay. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verses 13–14:

{13} This begins the detailed account of their story, and that Allah relates it to His Prophet ﷺ with the truth and sincerity, in which there is no doubt or uncertainty in any respect. {Indeed, they were young men who believed in their Lord}: This is a plural of paucity (jam' al-qillah), which indicates that they were fewer than ten. They believed in Allah alone, with no partner, apart from their people. So Allah thanked them for their faith and increased them in guidance. That is: because of the root of their being guided to faith, Allah increased them in guidance, which is beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds; as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah increases in guidance those who are guided﴾.

{14} {And We strengthened their hearts}; that is, We made them patient, firm, and We made their hearts content in that distressing situation. This is from His kindness and benevolence toward them, that He granted them success in faith, guidance, patience, steadfastness and tranquility. {When they stood up and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth}; that is, the One who created us, provided for us, managed us and nurtured us, is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the One who alone created these great creatures, not those idols and images, which create nothing, provide nothing, and possess no benefit, harm, death, life or resurrection. Thus they used the Lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah) as evidence for the Divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah). That is why they said: {We will never call upon any god besides Him}; that is, of all other creatures, {for then we would have spoken an enormity} – that is, if we called upon others along with Him after we knew that He is the Lord and the God, the only One deserving worship – {excess}; that is, a great deviation from the truth, and a path far from the correct. Thus they combined acknowledgment of tawhid al-rububiyyah and tawhid al-uluhiyyah, commitment to that, and a statement that this is the truth and whatever else is falsehood. This is evidence of the perfection of their knowledge of their Lord and the increase of guidance from Allah for them.

{15} When they had mentioned what Allah had bestowed upon them of faith, guidance and piety, they turned to what their people were upon of taking deities besides Allah. So they despised them and made clear that they were not certain of their affair; rather, they were in the utmost ignorance and misguidance. Thus they said: ﴿Why do they not bring for them a clear authority?﴾ That is: with a proof and an argument for what they are upon of falsehood. And they are unable to find any path to that. Rather, that is nothing but a fabrication against Allah and a lie upon Him, and this is the greatest wrong. Therefore He said: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾

{16} That is: some of them said to the others: since you have withdrawn from your people, both in their bodies and their religions, there remains only escape from their evil and taking the means that lead to that; for there is no way for them to fight against them, nor to remain among them while they are upon a religion other than theirs. ﴿Then take refuge in the cave﴾; that is, join together in it and hide yourselves in it. ﴿Your Lord will spread for you of His mercy and will prepare for you a means of ease in your affair﴾.

And previously He related that they supplicated Him by saying: ﴿Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us right guidance in our affair﴾. So they combined disavowal of their people and their power with turning to God for the rectification of their affair and supplicating Him for that, along with trust in God that He would do that. Indeed, God spread for them of His mercy and prepared for them a means of ease in their affair; He preserved their religions and their bodies, made them among His signs to His creation, and spread for them good praise, which is of His mercy toward them, and facilitated for them every means. Even the place in which they slept was in the utmost state of protection that is possible. Therefore He said:

{17} That is, Allah protected them from the sun. He made a cave easy for them such that when the sun rose it inclined away from them to the right, and when it set it passed them on the left, so its heat did not reach them and their bodies were not harmed by it. ﴿And they were in a spacious area within it﴾; that is, within the cave, a wide place. This was so that air and breeze would reach them, and the stuffiness and discomfort of a narrow place would be removed from them, especially with a long stay. ﴿That is among the signs of Allah﴾, which point to His power, His mercy, His answering of their supplication, and His guidance of them, even in these matters. For this reason He said: ﴿Whoever Allah guides is the one guided﴾; that is, there is no way to attain guidance except from Allah. He is the Guide who directs to the interests of both worlds. ﴿And whoever He leaves astray, you will never find for him a guiding protector﴾; that is, you will not find anyone who will take charge of him and manage his affairs in the way that is good for him, nor guide him to good and success, because Allah has decreed his misguidance, and none can repel His decree.

{18} ﴿And you would think them awake while they are asleep﴾; that is, you, O observer, would think they were awake, while in fact they were asleep. The commentators said: this is because their eyes were kept open so that they would not decay. So the one who looks at them thinks they are awake while they are asleep. ﴿And We turned them to the right and to the left﴾: this is also part of His protection of their bodies, because the earth by its nature consumes the bodies in contact with it. So it was by Allah's decree that He turned them onto their sides, to the right and to the left, to an extent that the earth would not corrupt their bodies. Allah, exalted is He, is able to protect them from the earth without turning them, but He is Wise, and He willed that His sunnah (established way) in creation should operate and that causes be tied to their effects. ﴿And their dog stretched out its forelegs at the threshold﴾; that is, the dog that was with the companions of the cave was overtaken by the sleep that overtook them during its guarding, so it was stretching its forelegs at the threshold, that is, the door or its courtyard. This is their protection from the earth. As for their protection from people, He informed that He shielded them with the awe that Allah cast over them. So if anyone had looked upon them, his heart would have been filled with terror and he would have turned away from them in flight. This is what caused them to remain for this long period while no one came upon them, despite their being very close to the city. The evidence of their closeness is that when they awoke, they sent one of them to buy food for them from the city, and they remained waiting for his return, which indicates how very close they were to it.

{19} Almighty Allah says: {And thus We raised them up} from their long sleep, {that they might question one another} — that is, that they might discuss among themselves in order to arrive at the truth regarding the length of their stay. {A speaker among them said, "How long have you remained?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day."} This is based on the speaker's assumption, as though confusion had arisen among them concerning the length of their sleep. Therefore {they said, "Your Lord knows best how long you have remained."} They referred the knowledge back to the One whose knowledge encompasses everything, in totality and in detail. Perhaps Allah afterward informed them of the length of their stay, since He raised them up {that they might question one another}, and He reported that they did question and speak according to what they had; yet their final state remained confusion. Therefore He must have informed them with certainty. We know this from His wisdom in raising them, and that He does not act in vain, and from His mercy toward whoever seeks knowledge of the truth in matters whose knowledge is sought and strives for it as far as he is able; for Allah makes that clear to him. This is also shown by His words that follow: {And thus We caused them to be found, that they might know that the promise of Allah is true and that the Hour — there is no doubt about it.} Had they not gained knowledge of their condition, they would not have been a proof of what was mentioned. Then, when they had questioned one another and what Allah reported had taken place among them, they sent one of them with their silver ({wariq}), that is, the coins they had with them, to buy them food to eat from the town from which they had come out, and they instructed him to choose the purest food, {azka}, that is, the best and most delicious, and to be gentle in his going, buying and returning, and to conceal himself in this and hide the condition of his companions, and not let anyone become aware of them.

{20} They mentioned the danger of others gaining knowledge of them and discovering them, that they were between two matters: either being stoned to death, whereby they would be killed in the most grievous manner, out of their rage against them and against their religion; or that they would tempt them away from their religion and return them to their creed. In that case, {you would never succeed}, but would instead lose in their religion, their worldly life and their hereafter.

These two verses indicate several benefits:
Among them: the exhortation to knowledge and to discussion about it, since Allah raised them for this purpose.
Among them: the courtesy of one who is confused about knowledge to refer it to its Knower and to stop at his limit.
Among them: the validity of agency (wakalah) in buying and selling, and the validity of partnership in that.
Among them: the permissibility of eating good foods and delicious provisions, provided it does not exceed the bounds of extravagance (israf) which is forbidden, based on His words: {So let him look at which is the purest food and bring you provision from it.} Especially when a person is not suited except by that. Perhaps this is the main basis of many exegetes who said that these were sons of kings, since they instructed him to choose the purest foods which the habit of great wealthy people is to consume.
Among them: the exhortation to caution, concealment, and keeping away from the places of trials in religion, and employing secrecy in that for oneself and for one's brothers in religion.
Among them: the intense desire of these youths for religion, their flight from every trial in their religion, and their leaving their homelands for the sake of Allah.
Among them: the mention of what evil contains of harms and corruptions that call for hating and abandoning it, and that this method is the method of the earlier and later believers, based on their words: {And you would never succeed then, ever.}

{21} He (Exalted is He) informs that He made the people aware of the condition of the People of the Cave. This was, and God knows best, after they had awakened and sent one of them to buy food for them, and they had instructed him to remain concealed and discreet. God willed a matter containing benefit for the people and an increase in reward for them: the people saw from them a sign of God's signs, witnessed with their own eyes, that God's promise is true, without doubt, without dispute, and without remoteness. This was after they had been disputing among themselves about their affair: some affirmed the promise and the recompense, and some denied that. So their story became an increase in insight and certainty for the believers and a proof against the deniers. They received the reward for this matter, God made their affair known and raised their station, until those who became aware of them held them in great esteem. They said: {Build over them a structure}; God knows best about their condition and their outcome! And those who prevailed over their affair, and they were the ones who held authority, said: {We will surely take over them a place of worship}; that is, we will worship God Most High therein and remember through it their condition and what happened to them. This state is forbidden, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prohibited it and censured those who do it. Mention of it here does not indicate that it is not blameworthy, for the context concerns the People of the Cave and praising them, and these people reached the point of saying "build over them a place of worship" after the People of the Cave's intense fear of their people and their caution against being discovered; so the situation reached what you see.

And in this story is evidence that whoever flees with his religion from trials, God preserves him from them; whoever seeks well-being, God grants him well-being; whoever takes refuge in God, God shelters him and makes him a guidance for others; and whoever endures humiliation in His cause and seeking His good pleasure, the end of his affair and its consequence will be great honor from where he does not expect, and what is with God is better for the righteous.

{22} Almighty God informs us about the disagreement of the People of the Book concerning the number of the Companions of the Cave, a disagreement arising from their conjecture about the unseen and their speaking about what they do not know. They held three views concerning this. Some say: ﴿They are three, the fourth of them is their dog﴾; others say: ﴿They are five, the sixth of them is their dog﴾. Both of these views were followed by God's statement that this is conjecture about the unseen, which indicates their invalidity. Others say: ﴿They are seven, and the eighth of them is their dog﴾. This, God knows best, is the correct view, because God refuted the first two and did not refute this one, which indicates its soundness. This is one of the disagreements that has no benefit beneath it, and knowing their number brings no religious or worldly benefit to people. For this reason God, Exalted, said: ﴿Say: My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few﴾, meaning those who hit upon the truth and knew that they had done so. ﴿So do not argue﴾: dispute and contend ﴿concerning them except with an outward argument﴾; that is, one based on knowledge and certainty, which also yields some benefit. As for argument based on ignorance and conjecture about the unseen, or argument that yields no benefit, either the opponent is obstinate, or the matter is one of no importance and no religious benefit is gained by knowing it, such as the number of the Companions of the Cave and the like. For many debates and lengthy investigations into it waste time and affect the affection of hearts without benefit. ﴿And do not consult any of them﴾ concerning the People of the Cave, ﴿of them﴾, that is, of the People of the Book, ﴿any one﴾. This is because their discourse about them is built on conjecture about the unseen and on speculation that does not avail against the truth at all. Therefore there is evidence here for prohibiting seeking a fatwa from one who is not fit to give fatwas, either because he is deficient in the matter asked about, or because he does not care what he says and has no piety to restrain him. If seeking the opinion of this kind of person is forbidden, then giving fatwas is forbidden all the more so and with greater reason.

The verse also contains evidence that a person may be forbidden to be consulted on one matter but not another, so he may be consulted on what he is qualified for, unlike others. This is because God did not forbid consulting them absolutely; He only forbade consulting them about the story of the Companions of the Cave and what is similar to it.

{23} This prohibition, like others, although it has a specific cause and is directed at the Messenger (ﷺ), the address is general to all who are responsible. So Allah forbade the servant, regarding future matters, from saying: "Indeed, I will do that," without attaching to it the will of Allah (mashi'ah). This is because of the harm (mahdhur) in it, which is speaking about unseen future matters, about which one does not know whether he will do it or not, and whether it will come to be or not. It also involves attributing the act to the servant's own will independently, and that is a forbidden harm, because all will belongs to Allah: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills, the Lord of the worlds﴾. Moreover, mentioning the will of Allah brings ease and facilitation of the matter, the occurrence of blessing in it, and the servant's seeking help from his Lord.

{24} Since the servant is a human being who must forget to mention the will (of Allah), Allah commanded him to make the exception (istithna') afterward when he remembers, so that the desired goal is achieved and the harm is averted. From the generality of His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾, is derived the command to remember Allah at the time of forgetfulness, for it removes it and reminds the servant of what he had neglected. Likewise, the one who is heedless and forgetful of the remembrance of Allah is commanded to remember his Lord and not be among the heedless. And since the servant is in need of Allah for His granting him success in being correct and free from error in his words and deeds, Allah commanded him to say: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right guidance (rashad)﴾. So He commanded him to supplicate to Allah, to hope in Him, and to trust that He will guide him to the nearest paths that lead to right guidance. It is fitting for a servant whose condition is this, then who exerts his effort and spends his utmost capacity in seeking guidance and right direction, that he be granted success in that, that help come to him from his Lord, and that He keep him firm in all his affairs.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verses 25–26:

{25–26} When Allah forbade him to ask the People of the Book for a ruling concerning the People of the Cave, because they lacked knowledge of it, and since Allah is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the One who knows everything, He informed him of the length of their sleep, and that the knowledge of this is with Him alone, for it is from the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and the unseen of these is exclusive to Him. Whatever He informs about it through the tongues of His messengers is the certain truth about which there is no doubt, and whatever He does not make His messengers aware of, no one among creation knows it. And His saying: ﴿Hear and see Him﴾ is an expression of wonder at the perfection of His hearing and His sight and their encompassing of all that is heard and seen, after He had informed of the all-encompassing nature of His knowledge of all things known. Then He informed of His sole possession of general and specific guardianship. He is the Guardian who manages the whole of creation, and the Guardian of His believing servants, bringing them out of darkness into light, facilitating for them the ease (al-yusra), and keeping them away from hardship (al-`usra). Hence He said: ﴿They have no protector besides Him﴾; that is, He is the One who looked after the People of the Cave with His kindness and generosity, and did not entrust them to any of creation. ﴿And He does not make anyone share in His command﴾: this includes both the cosmic, decreed command (al-hukm al-kawni al-qadari) and the legislative, religious command (al-hukm al-shar'i al-dini), for He is the Judge over His creation in decree, destiny, creation and management, and the Judge over them by His command, His prohibition, His reward and His punishment.

Since He, exalted is He, has the unseen of the heavens and the earth, there is no path for any created being to it except through the way by which He informs His servants. This Qur'an has comprised many unseen matters, so Allah commanded that one turn to it, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verse 27:

{27} Al-tilawa (recitation) means following. That is: follow what Allah has revealed to you, by knowing its meanings, understanding them, affirming its reports as true, and carrying out its commands and prohibitions. For it is the Glorious Book, whose words none can change (la mubaddil li-kalimatihi); that is, they cannot be altered or substituted, because of their truthfulness, their justice, and their attaining a goodness beyond every limit. ﴿And the word of your Lord is fulfilled in truth and justice﴾. Because of its perfection, alteration and substitution are impossible for it; if it were deficient, that or some part of it would befall it. In this there is an exaltation of the Qur'an, which implicitly encourages turning towards it. ﴿And you will never find apart from Him a refuge﴾; that is, you will not find, apart from your Lord, a shelter to which you can turn or a refuge in which you can seek protection. When it is established that He alone is the refuge in all matters, it is established that He is the one worshipped (al-ma'luh), the one to whom one turns in hardship and in ease, the one needed in all circumstances, and the one asked in all needs.

{28} God commands His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and others besides him as exemplars in commands and prohibitions, to restrain himself along with the believers who worship and turn penitently to Him: {Those who call upon their Lord morning and evening}; that is, at the beginning and end of the day, desiring thereby the countenance of God. He described them with worship and sincerity in it. In this is the command to keep company with the righteous and to struggle against the self to associate and mix with them, even if they are poor, for in their company are benefits that cannot be counted. {And let not your eyes overlook them}; that is, do not pass beyond them with your sight or turn your gaze away from them, {desiring the adornment of the worldly life}. For this is harmful and not beneficial, and it cuts one off from religious interests, since it necessitates the heart's attachment to this world, so that thoughts and preoccupations turn toward it, and the desire for the Hereafter departs from the heart. The adornment of this world pleases the beholder and bewitches the heart, so the heart becomes heedless of the remembrance of God and turns toward pleasures and desires, so its time is wasted, its affair falls into disorder, and it suffers the everlasting loss and the perpetual regret. For this reason He said: {And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance}: he was heedless of God, so God punished him by making him heedless of His remembrance. {And follows his desire}; that is, he became a follower of his desire, doing whatever his self craves and striving to attain it, even if it be his ruin and loss. He has taken his own desire as his god, as God, exalted is He, said: {Have you seen one who takes his desire as his god, and God misguides him knowingly...} [45:23], to the end of the verse. {And his affair has been [left] neglected}; that is, the interests of his religion and his worldly life are lost and idle. God has forbidden obeying such a person, because obedience to him calls to imitating him, and because he only calls to what he himself is characterized by.

The verse indicates that the one who deserves to be obeyed and to be an imam for the people is the one whose heart is filled with love of God, whose effect overflows onto his tongue, so he is constant in the remembrance of God, follows the things pleasing to his Lord, and puts them before his desire. Thereby he preserves what he preserves of his time, his conditions are sound, and his actions are upright, and he calls the people to what God has bestowed upon him. Such a person is truly worthy to be followed and made an imam.

The patience mentioned in this verse is patience in obedience to God, which is the highest kind of patience, and with its perfection the remaining categories are completed.

In the verse is the recommendation of remembrance, supplication, and worship at the two ends of the day, because God praised them for doing it, and every act for which God praises its doer indicates that God loves it; and when He loves it, He commands it and encourages it.

{29} He says: {Say} to the people, O Muhammad: {The truth is from your Lord}; that is, guidance has been made clear from misguidance, right conduct from error, and the attributes of the people of happiness from the attributes of the people of wretchedness, and that is through what Allah has made clear on the tongue of His Messenger. When it has become evident and manifest, and no doubt remains in it, then {whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve}; that is, nothing remains but the servant's taking one of the two paths, according to his being granted success or not being granted success. Allah has given him a will by which he is able to believe or disbelieve, to do good or evil. So whoever believes has been guided to what is correct, and whoever disbelieves, the proof has been established against him, and he is not compelled to believe, as Allah the Exalted said: {There is no compulsion in religion; the right course has become distinct from error} [al-Baqarah 2:256]. [And there is nothing in His saying: {whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve} that permits both matters; rather, it is a threat and a warning to whoever chooses disbelief after complete clarification, just as it does not imply abandoning the fight against the disbelievers.] Then He, the Exalted, mentioned the end of the two groups, saying: {Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers}: by disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience, {a Fire whose enclosure will surround them}; that is, its surrounding wall, so there is for them no outlet, no path, and no escape from it, {to be burned by the blazing Fire}. {And if they ask for relief}; that is, they seek drink to quench the intense thirst that has befallen them, {they will be relieved with water like murky oil}; that is, like molten lead, or like the dregs of oil, because of its intense heat. {It scalds the faces}; that is, how then the intestines and bellies? As Allah the Exalted said: {By which will be melted what is in their bellies and [their] skins. And for them are maces of iron} [al-Hajj 22:20–21]. {Wretched is the drink}, which is meant to quench thirst and relieve some of the torment, but it becomes an increase in their torment and the severity of their punishment. {And evil is the resting place}: the Fire. This is a censure of the state of the Fire: that it is an evil place of resting, for there is no resting in it; rather, in it is the great, arduous torment, which is not lightened for them for an hour, and they are in it in despair, having lost hope in every good, and the Merciful has forgotten them in the punishment just as they forgot Him.

{30} Then He mentioned the second group, saying: {Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds}; that is, they combined belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, its good and its evil, with the doing of righteous deeds, both obligatory and recommended. {Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of one who does good in deeds}: The excellence of deeds is that the servant intends the deed for the sake of Allah's countenance, following in that the law of Allah. So Allah does not waste this deed, nor any part of it; rather, He preserves it for its doers and gives them their reward in accordance with their deeds, His bounty, and His excellence.

{31} He mentioned their reward by His saying: {Those will have gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein on adorned couches}. [Those]: that is, those described with faith and righteous deeds, for them are the lofty gardens whose trees have multiplied, shading whoever is in them, and whose rivers have multiplied, flowing beneath those graceful trees and elevated dwellings. Their adornment therein is gold, and their clothing therein is green silk of sundus, which is the thick kind of brocade, and istabraq, which is the thinner kind of it. They recline therein on couches, which are adorned thrones decorated with fine garments; for it is not called a arika (couch) unless it is so. Their reclining on the couches indicates complete ease, the removal of fatigue and exhaustion, and that servants attend upon them, giving them whatever they desire, and the completion of that is eternal abiding and everlasting residence. This is the noble abode. {Excellent is the reward}: for the doers, {and good is the resting place}: they rest therein and enjoy what is in it of what the souls desire and the eyes delight in, of joy, happiness, lasting delight, successive pleasures, and abundant blessings. And what resting place is better than an abode whose lowest inhabitant wanders in his kingdom, bounty, palaces, and gardens for two thousand years? He sees nothing above what he is in of bliss; he has been given all his wishes and desires, and additional desires beyond what wishes could reach. Along with that, their bliss is perpetual, increasing in its qualities and beauty. We ask Allah the Generous not to deprive us of the best of what is with Him of benevolence because of the worst of what is with us of shortcoming and disobedience. This noble verse and what is similar to it show that adornment is general for males and females, as reported in the authentic traditions, because He stated it absolutely in His saying: {they will be adorned}; and likewise silk and the like.

{32} God, Exalted is He, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): Present to the people the parable of these two men: the one who is grateful for God's blessing and the one who disbelieves in it, and what proceeded from each of them of words and deeds, and what resulted from that of immediate and deferred punishment and reward, so that they may take a lesson from their condition and be admonished by what befell them. Knowing the specific identities of the two men, or at what time or place they lived, is of no benefit or consequence; the lesson is derived from their story alone, and dwelling on anything beyond that is overstepping (al-takalluf).

Of these two men, the one who disbelieved in God's great blessing, God had made for him two gardens; that is, two beautiful orchards {of grapevines, and We surrounded them with date palms}. That is, in these two gardens there were fruits of every kind, and especially the most noble trees, the grapevine and the date palm. The grapevine was in their midst, and the date palm encircled them and surrounded them. Thus there was in them beauty of appearance and splendor, and the trees and palms were exposed to the sun and the winds, by which the fruits are perfected, ripen, and attain their essence. Moreover, He placed between those trees cultivated crops (zar').

{33} Nothing remained for them except to be asked: how are the fruits of these two gardens, and do they have water sufficient for them? So God informed that each of {the two gardens yielded its produce}; that is, its fruit and crops, doubled; that is, multiplied, and that it {did not fail in anything}; that is, it did not diminish its produce in the least. Moreover, the rivers flowed abundantly and copiously along their sides.

{34} And he had fruit (thamar); that is, abundant fruit, as the indefinite form indicates. That is: both his gardens had brought their fruit to full maturity, their trees had grown abundant, and no blight or deficiency had befallen them. This was the ultimate extent of the adornment of this world in cultivation. For this reason, this man was deceived, grew arrogant, boasted, and forgot his Hereafter.

That is, the owner of the two gardens said to his companion, the believer, while they were conversing, that is, discussing between themselves some ordinary matters, boasting over him: ﴿I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in followers﴾. He took pride in the abundance of his wealth and the might of his supporters, from slaves, servants and relatives. This was ignorance on his part. {40} "Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and will send upon it" — that is, upon your garden, in which you became arrogant and which deceived you — "a calamity from heaven" — that is, a punishment in the form of a great rain or something else. "So that it becomes" — as a result of that — "a barren, slippery ground": its trees have been uprooted, its fruit destroyed, its crops drowned, and its benefit gone.

{41} "Or its water (from which it is fed) sinks into the earth" — that is, sinks deep into the ground — "so that you will never be able to find it." That is, it sinks so deep that it cannot be reached with tools or otherwise. He (the believer) invoked this upon the garden out of anger for his Lord, because it had deceived its owner, made him rebellious, and he had become content with it; perhaps he would repent, return to his right guidance, and reflect upon his affair.

{42} So God answered his supplication, and "his fruit was encompassed" — that is, a punishment befell him that encompassed it and destroyed it, so that nothing remained of it. Encompassing the fruit necessarily entails the destruction of all his trees, fruit, and crops. So he regretted with the utmost regret, and his grief intensified over it. "Then he began to wring his hands over what he had spent upon it" — that is, over the great worldly expenses he had lavished on it, since it was ruined and perished, leaving no compensation for it — and he also regretted his polytheism and his evil. For this reason he said: "Would that I had not associated anyone with my Lord!"

{43} God the Exalted said: "And he had no company to help him against God, nor could he help himself." That is, when the punishment descended upon his garden, what he used to boast of, his saying to his companion, "I have more wealth than you and greater support in men," departed from him. They did not ward off from him any of the punishment, though he was in greatest need of them, and he could not help himself. How could he be helped, or have any means of victory, against God's decree and destiny, which, once He has enacted and decreed it, even if the people of the heavens and the earth gathered to remove any part of it, they would not be able to do so? {45} Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet ﷺ primarily, and to whoever inherits his role after him secondarily:

Set forth for the people ﴿the parable of the worldly life﴾, so that they may picture it as it truly is, know its outward and inward aspects, compare it with the everlasting abode, and prefer whichever of the two deserves to be preferred. The likeness of this worldly life is like rain that descends from the sky upon the earth, so that the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and it brings forth every beautiful pair. Then, while its blossom and its adornment delight the onlookers, gladden the spectators, and captivate the heedless, suddenly it becomes ﴿dry stubble which the winds scatter﴾. That flourishing vegetation, that bright blossom, and that lovely sight are gone, and the earth becomes dusty, a mere dry dust from which the gaze has turned away and the eye has been diverted, and which leaves the heart desolate. So it is with this world. While its possessor is admiring his youth, surpassing his peers and contemporaries in it, gathering its dirhams and dinars, plucking the flowers of its pleasures, plunging into its desires at all times, and thinking that he will remain in it for all his days, suddenly death or the loss of his wealth overtakes him. Then his joy departs, his pleasure and delight cease, his heart becomes desolate with pains, and he parts from his youth, his strength, and his wealth, and is left alone with his good or evil deeds. At that moment ﴿the wrongdoer will bite his hands﴾ when he comes to know the reality of his condition, and he wishes to return to the world, not in order to complete his desires, but in order to make up for the heedlessness he committed, through repentance and righteous deeds. Therefore the wise, resolute, and successful person presents this state to himself and says to his soul: "Imagine that you have died, and you must surely die. Which of the two states will you choose: being deceived by the adornment of this abode and enjoying it like the enjoyment of grazing livestock, or working for an abode whose fruit is everlasting and whose shade endures, and in which is what the souls desire and the eyes delight in?" By this, the success of the servant is distinguished from his abandonment, and his profit from his loss.

{46} For this reason Allah the Exalted informed that wealth and children are ﴿the adornment of the worldly life﴾; that is, there is nothing beyond that. And that what remains for a person, benefits him, and gladdens him is ﴿the enduring good deeds﴾. This includes all obligatory and recommended acts of worship, both those concerning the rights of Allah and those concerning the rights of His servants: prayer, zakat, charity, Hajj, 'Umrah, glorifying God (tasbih), praising Him (tahmid), declaring His oneness (tahlil), [magnifying Him (takbir)], recitation, seeking beneficial knowledge, enjoining what is good, forbidding what is evil, maintaining ties of kinship, kindness to parents, fulfilling the rights of wives, slaves, and animals, and all forms of benevolence to creation. All of this is among ﴿the enduring good deeds﴾. These are ﴿better in reward with your Lord and better in hope﴾, for their reward remains and multiplies for ages, and their benefit, kindness, and usefulness are hoped for at times of need. These are the things that those who compete should compete for, that those who strive should hasten toward, and that those who labor should earnestly seek to attain.

Reflect on how, when Allah set forth the parable of the world, its condition, and its perishing, He mentioned that what is in it is of two kinds: one kind of its adornment, which is enjoyed for a little while and then passes away without any benefit returning to its possessor, rather harm may even befall him, and that is wealth and children; and another kind which remains for its possessor forever, and that is ﴿the enduring good deeds﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verse 47–49:

{47 – 48} He, exalted is He, informs about the state of the Day of Resurrection and the terrors within it, the disturbing distresses and the unsettling hardships. He says: {And the Day We will set the mountains in motion}; that is, He will remove them from their places, make them into scattered sand-dunes, then make them like carded wool, then they will be crushed and dispersed and become scattered dust. The earth will be laid bare, becoming a smooth level plain in which there is no crookedness and no elevation. Allah will gather all creation upon that earth, leaving none of them behind. He will gather the first and the last from the depths of the wastelands and the bottoms of the seas, gathering them after they had been scattered and restoring them after they had been torn apart, as a new creation. {And they will be presented before your Lord in rows}, so that He may review them and look into their deeds and judge them with His just judgment, in which there is no injustice or wrong. He will say to them: {You have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time}; that is, without wealth, without family, without kin. With them there will be only the deeds they performed and the gains, good and evil, that they earned, as Allah, exalted is He, says: {And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners [in Allah]} (6:94). He says here, addressing those who denied the resurrection after having witnessed it with their own eyes: {Rather, you claimed that We would not appoint for you an appointment}; that is, you denied the recompense for deeds and the promise and threat of Allah. So now you have seen it and tasted it.

{49} Then the books of deeds will be brought forth, which the noble angels had written. Hearts will flutter with fear because of them, the distresses will grow heavy by their impact, and even the hard, solid rocks will be nearly melted by them. The criminals will be fearful of them. When they see them, with their deeds inscribed against them and their words and actions counted against them, they will say: {Woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it!} That is, it leaves out no minor or major sin without it being recorded therein and preserved; nothing of secret or open deeds, nor of night or day, has been forgotten from it. {And they will find what they did present}: they cannot deny it. {And your Lord does not wrong anyone}: then they will be recompensed for it, made to acknowledge it, be disgraced, and the punishment will become due upon them. {That is because of what your hands have put forth, and because Allah is not ever unjust to the servants} (8:51 style): rather, they are not outside His justice and His bounty.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verse 50:

{50} He (exalted is He) informs us of the enmity of Iblis toward Adam and his offspring, and that Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, honoring and glorifying him and complying with the command of Allah, so they complied with that. {Except Iblis. He was of the jinn, so he defied the command of his Lord}, and he said: {Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?} And he said: {I am better than him}. Thereby his enmity toward Allah and toward your father is made clear. So how could you take him {and his offspring}, i.e., the devils, {as allies instead of Me, while they are an enemy to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers}, i.e.:

{Wretched is what they have chosen for themselves}: the guardianship of Satan, who does not command them except to indecency and wrongdoing, instead of the guardianship of the Most Merciful, in whose guardianship lies all happiness, success and joy. In this verse there is an exhortation to take Satan as an enemy and an incitement to that, together with mention of the reason that necessitates it, and that none does this except a wrongdoer. And what greater wrong is there than the wrong of one who takes his true enemy as an ally and abandons the Praiseworthy Protector?! Allah, exalted is He, said: {Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light. And those who disbelieve, their protectors are the Taghut; they bring them out of the light into darkness}, and He, exalted is He, said: {Indeed, they have taken the devils as protectors instead of Allah}.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verses 51–52:

{51} He, exalted is He, says: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves.﴾ That is: I did not cause them to be present for that, nor did I consult them about it. So how could they be creators of anything of that? Rather, the One who alone creates, governs, and possesses wisdom and decree is Allah, the Creator of all things, who disposes of them by His wisdom. How, then, could partners among the devils be assigned to Him, who are befriended and obeyed as Allah is obeyed, when they have not created, have not witnessed any creation, and have not assisted Allah, the Exalted? For this reason He says: ﴿Nor would I take the misleaders as helpers (ʿaḍud)﴾. That is: as aides supporting Allah in any matter. That is: it is not fitting or proper for Allah to give them any share in the management (of affairs), because they are busy misguiding creation and are hostile to their Lord. Rather, what is fitting is that He keep them far away and not bring them near.

{52} When He had mentioned the state of those who associated others with Him in this world, and had refuted this association in the utmost refutation, and had judged its adherent to be ignorant and foolish, He informed of their situation with their partners on the Day of Resurrection, and that Allah will say to them: ﴿Call upon My partners, whom you claimed.﴾ That is: according to your corrupt assumption; otherwise, in reality, Allah has no partner on earth or in heaven. That is: call upon them so that they may benefit you and rescue you from the severe hardships. ﴿But they will call upon them, and they will not respond to them.﴾ Because judgment and dominion on that Day belong entirely to Allah; no one possesses even an atom's weight of benefit, either for himself or for others. ﴿And We will place between them﴾ — that is, between the polytheists and their partners — ﴿a barrier (mawbiq)﴾: that is, a place of destruction which separates them from one another and distances some of them from others, and at that time the enmity of the partners toward their worshippers will become manifest, along with their disbelief in them and their disavowal of them, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship.﴾

For this reason He says: ﴿Nor would I take the misleaders as helpers (ʿaḍud)﴾. That is: as aides supporting Allah in any matter. That is: it is not fitting or proper for Allah to give them any share in the management (of affairs), because they are busy misguiding creation and are hostile to their Lord. Rather, what is fitting is that He keep them far away and not bring them near.

{52} When He had mentioned the state of those who associated others with Him in this world, and had refuted this association in the utmost refutation, and had judged its adherent to be ignorant and foolish, He informed of their situation with their partners on the Day of Resurrection, and that Allah will say to them: ﴿Call upon My partners, whom you claimed.﴾ That is: according to your corrupt assumption; otherwise, in reality, Allah has no partner on earth or in heaven. That is: call upon them so that they may benefit you and rescue you from the severe hardships. ﴿But they will call upon them, and they will not respond to them.﴾ Because judgment and dominion on that Day belong entirely to Allah; no one possesses even an atom's weight of benefit, either for himself or for others. ﴿And We will place between them﴾ — that is, between the polytheists and their partners — ﴿a barrier (mawbiq)﴾: that is, a place of destruction which separates them from one another and distances some of them from others, and at that time the enmity of the partners toward their worshippers will become manifest, along with their disbelief in them and their disavowal of them, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship.﴾

{53} That is: when the Day of Resurrection comes, and the reckoning takes place, and every group of creation is distinguished by its deeds, and the word of punishment is due upon the criminals, they will see Hell before entering it, and they will be alarmed, and their anxiety will intensify, because they will think that they are going to fall into it. The commentators said that this "thinking" (ẓann) here carries the meaning of certainty (yaqīn), so they will be certain that they are going to enter it. {And they will not find any escape from it} — that is, no alternative they could turn to, and no intercessor for them except by His permission. In this there is such warning and admonition that hearts and minds tremble.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verse 54:

{54} He, exalted is He, informs of the greatness, majesty and comprehensiveness of the Qur'an, and that He has diversified in it ﴿every kind of example﴾; that is, every path that leads to beneficial knowledge and everlasting happiness, and every path that protects from evil and destruction. Thus it contains examples of the permissible (halal) and the forbidden (haram), the recompense for deeds, encouragement (tarhib... wa-tarhib) and warning, and true, beneficial reports for the hearts, in belief, tranquility and light. This is what necessitates submission to this Qur'an, receiving it with compliance and obedience, and not disputing it in any matter. Despite this, many people argue about the truth after it has become clear, and they argue with falsehood in order to refute the truth thereby. Hence He said: ﴿But man is most of all things given to disputation﴾; that is, to argument and contention concerning it, even though such conduct is neither fitting for them nor just on their part. What caused them to do this, and to not believe in God, is nothing but wrongdoing and obstinacy, not any deficiency in its exposition, its proof or its demonstration. Otherwise, if the punishment came to them and what came before them came to them, their state would not be this. Hence He said:

{55} That is: what prevented people from believing, while the guidance by which the distinction between right guidance and misguidance, and between truth and falsehood, is attained, had already reached them and the proof of Allah had been established against them, was not the lack of clarification. Rather, what prevented them from belief was injustice and transgression. Nothing remained except that there come upon them the sunnah of Allah (His established way) and His practice with the earlier peoples: that when they do not believe, they are hastened with punishment, or they see the punishment approaching them, face to face and in plain view. That is: let them fear that, and let them repent of their disbelief before there comes the punishment that cannot be turned back.

{56} That is: We did not send the Messengers in vain, nor so that people would take them as lords, nor so that they would call people to themselves. Rather, We sent them calling people to every good and forbidding every evil, giving them glad tidings, for obeying that, of reward in this world and the next, and warning them, for disobeying that, of punishment in this world and the next. Thereby the proof of Allah was established against the servants. Yet, despite that, the wrongdoers and disbelievers refuse except to dispute with falsehood in order to refute the truth. So they strive to support falsehood as much as they can, and to repel and nullify the truth, and they mock the messengers of Allah and His signs, and they rejoice in the knowledge they have. ﴿And Allah refuses except that He perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it﴾, and the truth prevails over falsehood. ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes﴾. And among the wisdom and mercy of Allah is that His permitting the falsifiers who dispute truth with falsehood is among the greatest means to the clarity of the truth and the manifestation of its signs and proofs, and the manifestation of falsehood and its corruption; for by their opposites are things made clear.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verses 57–59:

{57} He, may He be exalted, informs that there is no one more unjust nor greater in crime than a servant who is reminded of the signs of Allah, to whom the truth is made clear from falsehood and guidance from misguidance, who is warned, frightened and encouraged, yet turns away from them, does not take heed from what he has been reminded of, and does not return from what he was upon. {And forgets what his hands have put forward} of sins, and does not fear the Knower of the unseen. This one is more unjust than the one who turns away and to whom the signs of Allah have not come and who has not been reminded of them; even if the latter is also unjust, the former is more unjust than him, because the sinner who has insight and knowledge is greater in sin than one who is not like that. But Allah, may He be exalted, punishes him, because of his turning away from His signs, his forgetting of his sins, and his contentment with himself in a state of evil while knowing it, by closing off for him the doors of guidance, by placing over his heart coverings (akinnah), that is, firm veils that prevent him from understanding the signs even if he hears them; so it is not within his capacity to comprehend in a way that reaches the heart. {And in their ears is deafness} (wiqr), that is, a deafness that prevents them from the signs reaching them and from hearing them in a way that benefits them; and even if they are in this condition, there is no path to their guidance. {And if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever} (idhan abadan): because the one from whom one may hope that he will respond to the caller to guidance is the one who is not knowledgeable; as for these people who saw and then became blind, who recognized the path of truth and abandoned it, and took the path of misguidance, and Allah punished them by locking their hearts and sealing them, there is no means or path to their guidance. In this verse there is a warning to whoever abandons the truth after knowing it, that there will be placed between him and it (a barrier), and he will not be able thereafter to attain it, which is the greatest deterrent and restraint from that.

{58} Then He, may He be exalted, informs of the vastness of His forgiveness and mercy, and that He forgives sins and accepts repentance from whoever repents, enfolding him with His mercy and encompassing him with His kindness; and that if He were to take the servants to account for what their hands have put forward of sins, He would hasten the punishment for them. But He, may He be exalted, is Forbearing and does not hasten to punishment; rather He gives respite and does not neglect. Sins must have their consequences, even if those consequences are delayed for a long time. Therefore He said: {Rather, for them there is an appointment; they will never find from other than it a refuge}: that is, for them there is an appointment at which they will be recompensed for their deeds; they must meet it, there is no escape from it, and no shelter or refuge from it.

{59} This is His way with the former and latter peoples: that He does not hasten punishment upon them, but rather invites them to repentance and turning back to Him. If they repent and turn back, He forgives them, shows them mercy, and removes punishment from them. Otherwise, if they persist in their wrongdoing and obstinacy, and the time He set as their appointment comes, He sends His might upon them. Therefore He said: {And those cities—We destroyed them when they wronged}: that is, because of their wrongdoing, not by any wrong from Us. {And We made for their destruction an appointment}: that is, a specified time from which they neither advance nor delay.
