He was given the choice between the two matters, because the apparent situation is that they were either disbelievers, or wicked, or had some of that quality; for if they had been believers who were not wicked, he would not have been permitted to punish them.

{87} So Dhu al-Qarnayn exercised the legitimate governance by which he deserved praise and commendation, due to Allah's granting him success in that. He said: I will divide them into two groups. ﴿As for one who wrongs﴾, by disbelief, ﴿we will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾; that is, he will receive two punishments: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

{88} ﴿But as for one who believes and does righteousness, he will have a reward of the best﴾; that is, he will have Paradise and a good state with Allah as a reward on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And we will speak to him from Our command with ease﴾; that is, we will be kind to him, speak to him gently, and make his dealings easy. This indicates that he was one of the righteous kings and the just, knowledgeable guardians, since he conformed to the pleasure of Allah in dealing with each person according to what befits his condition.

{83} The People of the Book, or the polytheists, asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, so Allah commanded him to say: ﴿I will recite to you from him a remembrance﴾. There is in it useful information and a wondrous account; that is, I will recite to you from his circumstances what is worth remembering and what serves as a lesson. As for anything else of his circumstances, He did not recite it to them.

{84–85} ﴿Indeed, We established him in the earth﴾; that is, Allah granted him dominion and empowered him to exercise authority across the regions of the earth, and the people submitted to him. ﴿And We gave him of every thing a means. So he followed a means﴾; that is, Allah gave him the means that connected him to what he reached, by which he could aid himself in subduing lands and easily reaching the far ends of the inhabited world, and he acted upon those means which Allah had given him; that is, he used them in their proper manner. So when the capability to employ the true means is combined with acting upon it, the aim is achieved; and if either or both are absent, it is not achieved. {88} ﴿But as for one who believes and does righteousness, he will have a reward of the best﴾; that is, he will have Paradise and a good state with Allah as a reward on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And we will speak to him from Our command with ease﴾; that is, we will be kind to him, speak to him gently, and make his dealings easy. This indicates that he was one of the righteous kings and the just, knowledgeable guardians, since he conformed to the pleasure of Allah in dealing with each person according to what befits his condition.

{89} That is: when he reached the place where the sun sets, he turned back, heading toward its rising, following the means that Allah had given him.

{90} So he reached the place where the sun rises, and "found it rising over a people for whom We had made no shelter against it." That is: he found it rising over people who had no covering from the sun, either because they did not build dwellings, owing to their increased savagery, wildness and lack of civilization, or because the sun is perpetually over them and does not set [for them] in any noticeable way, as is found in the southern east of Africa. He thus reached a place that the knowledge of the people of the earth had lost track of, let alone their having reached it with their bodies.

{91} Yet all of this was by Allah's decree and His knowledge of it, and therefore He said: "Thus [it was], and We had encompassed with knowledge what was with him." That is: [We encompassed] what he possessed of goodness and great means, and Our knowledge was with him wherever he turned and traveled.

{92–93} "Then he followed a way, until, when he reached between the two barriers." The exegetes said: he went, heading from the east, intending the north, and reached the area between the two barriers. These were two barriers known in that era, two chains of mountains joined to the right and left until they connected with the seas, between Gog and Magog and the people. "He found beside them a people who scarcely could understand any speech," because of the foreignness of their tongues and the incomprehension of their minds and hearts.

{94} Allah had given Dhul-Qarnayn the means of knowledge by which he understood their languages, comprehended them, and they conversed with him and he with them. They complained to him of the harm of Gog and Magog, two great nations of the children of Adam. They said: "Indeed, Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land," through killing, seizing wealth, and other things. "So shall we pay you a tribute?" That is, a reward, "on condition that you build between us and them a barrier." This indicates that they were not capable by themselves of building the barrier, and they recognized Dhul-Qarnayn's power to do it, so they offered him a wage to do so, and mentioned to him the motive, namely their corruption in the land.

{95} Dhul-Qarnayn was not a man of greed or desire for worldly things, nor one who neglected the improvement of the affairs of his subjects; rather, his aim was reform. Therefore he answered their request, because of the benefit in it, and did not take a wage from them, and he thanked his Lord for His enabling and power. So he said to them: "What my Lord has established me in is better," that is, better than what you offer me and give me; I only ask of you that you help me with strength from your hands: "I will make between you and them a barrier," that is, a barrier preventing their crossing over you.

{96} "Bring me blocks of iron," that is, pieces of iron, and they gave him that. "Until, when he had leveled between the two cliffs," that is, the two mountains between which the barrier was built, "he said: Blow." That is, the fire: kindle it with great intensity and use bellows for it, so that it grows hot and melts the copper. When the copper that he wanted to fasten between the blocks of iron had melted, "he said: Bring me, I will pour over it molten copper," that is, molten brass, so he poured the molten metal over it, and the barrier became exceedingly firm, and those behind it were protected from the harm of Gog and Magog.

{97} "So they could not scale it, nor could they make a breach in it," that is, they had no ability or power to climb over it because of its height, nor to pierce it because of its solidity and strength.

{98} When he had done this noble deed and this great work, he attributed the blessing to its Giver and said: "This is a mercy from my Lord," that is, from His bounty and kindness toward me. This is the condition of the caliphs and the righteous: when Allah bestows great blessings upon them, their gratitude, acknowledgment and recognition of Allah's favor increase, as Sulayman (peace be upon him) said when the throne of the Queen of Sheba was brought before him from a great distance: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful." By contrast, for the people of tyranny, arrogance and haughtiness on the earth, great blessings only increase them in insolence and exultation, as Qarun said when Allah had given him treasures whose keys would weigh down a band of strong men: "I was only given it because of knowledge I possess." And His saying: "So when the promise of my Lord comes," that is, the emergence of Gog and Magog, "He will make it," that is, that barrier so firm and well-made, "levelled," that is, He will level it so that it collapses, and it will become even with the ground, "and the promise of my Lord is ever true."

{100} As for the disbelievers, despite their differences, Hell is their recompense, abiding therein forever. For this reason He said: ﴿And We will present Hell on that Day to the disbelievers, exposed﴾, just as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when Hellfire is ignited﴾. That is: it is displayed to them so that it becomes their abode and their dwelling place, and so that they may taste its shackles, its blaze, its boiling water, and its bitter cold, and so that they may experience of punishment that which renders the hearts speechless and deafens the ears.

{101} This is the consequence of their deeds and the recompense of their actions. For in the worldly life, their eyes were under a covering from the remembrance of Allah; that is, they turned away from the Wise Reminder and the Noble Qur'an. ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you call us"﴾, and in their eyes there were veils preventing them from seeing the beneficial signs of Allah, just as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And over their eyes is a veil﴾. ﴿And they were unable to hear﴾; that is, they were not able to hear the signs of Allah that lead to faith, because of their hatred of the Qur'an and the Messenger. For one who hates cannot bring himself to lend his hearing to the speech of one he hates. So when the paths of knowledge and goodness are blocked from them, they have no hearing, no sight, and no beneficial intellect. Thus they disbelieved in Allah, denied His signs, and rejected His messengers, so they deserved Hell, and "evil is it as a destination" (﴿وساءت مصيراً﴾).

{102} This is a proof and clarification of the invalidity of the claim of the idolatrous disbelievers who took some of the prophets and saints as partners with God, worshipping them, and claiming that they would be their protectors, rescuing them from the punishment of God and bestowing upon them His reward, while they themselves had disbelieved in God and His Messenger. God says to them, in the form of a rhetorical question expressing denial, whose invalidity is established in the intellects: ﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as protectors besides Me?﴾; meaning: that cannot be, and the friend of God never takes as a friend one who is an enemy of God, ever; for the friends of God agree with God in His love, His pleasure, His anger and His hatred. Thus, according to this meaning, it resembles His Exalted saying: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all and say to the angels, "Did these worship you?" They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our Protector, not them."﴾

So whoever claims that he takes the friend of God as his friend while he is an enemy of God, is a liar. It is also possible, and this is the apparent meaning, that the meaning is: Do the disbelievers, who deny God and oppose His messengers, think that they may take, besides God, protectors who will help them and benefit them besides God, and repel harm from them? This is a false assumption and a corrupt opinion, for all created beings have no power over benefit or harm. This is like His Exalted saying: ﴿Say, "Call upon those you claim besides Him; they do not possess the removal of harm from you or its transfer."﴾ And: ﴿And those they call upon besides Him do not possess intercession.﴾ And similar verses in which God mentions that whoever takes as a protector, besides Him, one who helps him and supports him, is astray, disappointed in hope, not attaining some of his aims.

﴿Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as an abode﴾; meaning: as hospitality and entertainment. How evil is the abode they have, and how evil is Hell as their hospitality.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verses 103–106:

{103} That is: Say, O Muhammad, to the people, as a warning and admonition: Shall I inform you of the greatest losers in (their) deeds, absolutely?

{104} {Those whose effort has gone astray in the life of this world}; that is, whatever deeds they did became null and void and perished, {while they think that they are doing good in their work}. So how about their deeds which they know to be false and which oppose and act hostilely against Allah and His messengers?!

{105} Who are these whose deeds have been lost, so that they have lost themselves on the Day of Resurrection and their families on the Day of Resurrection? Is that not the manifest loss? {Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him}; that is, they denied the Qur'anic signs and the observable signs that indicate the obligation of believing in Him, His angels, His messengers, His books and the Last Day. {So their deeds have become worthless}, because of that, {and We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight}: because the purpose of the weighing is to compare good deeds with bad deeds and to consider which of them outweighs and which is outweighed, and these people have no good deeds, due to the absence of their condition, which is faith; as Allah the Exalted said: {And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, then he will not fear injustice or diminution}. But their deeds will be counted and enumerated, they will be made to acknowledge them, and they will be disgraced by them before all witnesses, and then they will be punished for them.

{106} Therefore He said: {That is their recompense}; that is, the nullification of their deeds, and that no weight will be set up for them on the Day of Resurrection; because of their insignificance and baseness, through their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their taking His signs and His messengers in mockery, mocking and ridiculing them [therewith], whereas what is obligatory regarding the signs of Allah and His messengers is complete faith in them, glorifying them, and upholding them to the utmost degree. These people reversed the matter, so their affair was reversed, and they stumbled and fell headlong into the punishment.

When he had explained the end of the disbelievers and their deeds, he explained the deeds of the believers and their end, saying:

Is that not the manifest loss? {Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him}; that is, they denied the Qur'anic signs and the observable signs that indicate the obligation of believing in Him, His angels, His messengers, His books and the Last Day. {So their deeds have become worthless}, because of that, {and We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight}: because the purpose of the weighing is to compare good deeds with bad deeds and to consider which of them outweighs and which is outweighed, and these people have no good deeds, due to the absence of their condition, which is faith; as Allah the Exalted said: {And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, then he will not fear injustice or diminution}. But their deeds will be counted and enumerated, they will be made to acknowledge them, and they will be disgraced by them before all witnesses, and then they will be punished for them.

{106} Therefore He said: {That is their recompense}; that is, the nullification of their deeds, and that no weight will be set up for them on the Day of Resurrection; because of their insignificance and baseness, through their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their taking His signs and His messengers in mockery, mocking and ridiculing them [therewith], whereas what is obligatory regarding the signs of Allah and His messengers is complete faith in them, glorifying them, and upholding them to the utmost degree. These people reversed the matter, so their affair was reversed, and they stumbled and fell headlong into the punishment.

When he had explained the end of the disbelievers and their deeds, he explained the deeds of the believers and their end, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verses 107–108:

{107} That is: {Indeed, those who believed}: with their hearts,
{and did righteous deeds}: with their limbs. This description encompasses the whole of the religion: its beliefs and its actions, its fundamentals and its branches, the outward and the inward. Thus these, despite their differing ranks of faith and righteous action,
{for them are the Gardens of Paradise (Firdaws) as hospitality}. It is possible that what is meant by the Gardens of Firdaws is the highest part of Paradise, its middle and its best, and that this reward is for those who perfect faith and righteous action, namely the prophets and those brought near (to Allah). It is also possible that what is meant is all the dwelling-places of the Gardens, so that this reward encompasses all the ranks of the people of faith, from those brought near and the righteous to the moderate, each according to his state. This is the [more preferable] of the two meanings, because of its generality, and because Paradise is mentioned in the plural form, idafa'd to Firdaws, and because Firdaws is applied to a garden containing vineyards or dense trees, and this applies to the whole of Paradise. So the Garden of Firdaws is a lodging and hospitality for the people of faith and righteous action. And what hospitality could be greater, more magnificent and more sublime than this hospitality, which contains every kind of bliss for the hearts, the spirits and the bodies?! Therein is what the souls desire and what the eyes find delight in: elegant dwellings, flourishing meadows, fruitful trees, birds singing sweetly, delicious foods, pleasant drinks, beautiful women, servants and youths, flowing rivers, pleasing sights, sensory and spiritual beauty, and everlasting blessing. The highest, best and most sublime of all this is the enjoyment of nearness to the Most Merciful and attaining His pleasure, which is the greatest bliss of the Gardens, and the delight of beholding His noble Face and hearing the speech of the Compassionate, the Merciful. Glory be to Allah, how great, how beautiful, how lasting and how complete is that hospitality! It is greater than anyone among the creatures can encompass with description, or that can occur to the hearts. Were the servants to know some of that bliss with a true knowledge that reaches their hearts, their hearts would fly toward it with longing, their spirits would be torn apart by the pain of separation, and they would journey toward it in groups and individually, and they would not prefer over it a fleeting worldly life or troubled, vanishing pleasures, nor would they waste moments that pass away in loss, while every single moment of its bliss is worth thousands of ages. But heedlessness has overtaken them, faith has weakened, knowledge has diminished, and resolve has slackened, so what happened happened. There is no power and no might except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.

{108} And His saying: {abiding therein}: this is the
completion of bliss, that therein is complete bliss, and of its completeness is that it does not end. {they will not desire any transfer from it}; that is, no change and no removal, because they see only what pleases them, delights them, gladdens them and makes them joyful, and they see no bliss beyond what they are in.

{109} That is: Say to them, informing them of the greatness of the Creator and the vastness of His attributes, and that the servants cannot encompass any part of them: ﴿If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord﴾; that is, these seas that exist in the world; ﴿the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted﴾; that is, and the trees of this world, from its beginning to its end, from the trees of the lands, the deserts and the seas, were pens. And the pens would break, ﴿before the words of my Lord are exhausted﴾. This is a great matter that no one can encompass. In another verse: ﴿And if whatever trees on earth were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, [were ink], the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Almighty and Wise﴾. This is from the method of bringing the meaning closer to the minds, because these things are created, and all created things are finite and limited. As for the speech of Allah, it is one of His attributes, and His attributes are uncreated and have no limit and no end. Whatever vastness and greatness the hearts can imagine, Allah is above that. The same applies to all the attributes of Allah, such as His knowledge, His wisdom, His power and His mercy. If the knowledge of all creatures, of the first and the last, the people of the heavens and the people of the earth, were gathered together, it would be, compared to the knowledge of the Mighty, less than the proportion of a sparrow that alighted on the edge of the sea and took with its beak from the sea, compared to the sea and its greatness. That is because Allah possesses the great, vast and perfect attributes, and ﴿to your Lord is the final end﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 18, verse 110:

{110} That is: Say, O Muhammad, to the disbelievers and others: ﴿Verily, I am only a human being like you﴾; that is, I am not a god, nor do I have any partnership in the dominion, nor knowledge of the unseen, nor do I possess the treasuries of Allah. I am only a human being like you, a servant among the servants of my Lord. ﴿It is revealed to me that your God is but one God﴾; that is, I have been favoured over you with the revelation that Allah reveals to me, which is greatest in that it informs you, ﴿that your God is but one God﴾; that is, He has no partner, and no one deserves worship of even the weight of an atom other than Him. I call you to the deed that brings you close to Him, grants you His reward, and repels His punishment from you. For this reason He said: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds﴾, which is what conforms to the Law of Allah, whether obligatory or recommended, ﴿and let him not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾; that is, he should not show off in his deed, but should perform it sincerely for the sake of the Face of Allah, Exalted. This one who combines sincerity (ikhlas) and following the Prophet's way (mutaba'ah) is the one who attains what he hopes for and seeks. As for whoever departs from this, he is a loser in his worldly life and in the Hereafter, and he has missed nearness to his Master and attaining His pleasure.

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Kahf. All praise is due to Allah.
